subject.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup

question: Should startup ever automatically delete unowned legacy `openclaw-cli-mcp-*` directories when an older concurrent gateway may still have a queued run using them?
rationale: The repository's upgrade policy favors preserving live existing workflows, but omitting automatic legacy cleanup leaves previously leaked credential files for doctor or operator cleanup; that tradeoff requires an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Protect legacy directories
options.body: Reclaim owner-encoded directories automatically and move legacy cleanup to an explicit doctor or operator action, avoiding mixed-version queued-run breakage.

options.title: Accept heuristic legacy cleanup
options.body: Keep the age-plus-argv fallback only with explicit maintainer acceptance and real rolling-upgrade proof covering an older gateway's queued pre-spawn configuration.

recommendation.title: Protect legacy directories
recommendation.body: Reclaim owner-encoded directories automatically and move legacy cleanup to an explicit doctor or operator action, avoiding mixed-version queued-run breakage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged cleanup-lifecycle work is the strongest available history signal for deciding when bundled-MCP configurations cease being live.
